subject: Linguistics
title: Constructed Scripts
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Constructed Scripts.

hook.text: Tolkien didn't just invent Elvish languages—he created entire writing systems with their own histories.

buildup.text: Constructed scripts are writing systems deliberately designed for fictional or ideological purposes.

discovery.text: Klingon (Star Trek), Aurebesh (Star Wars), and Shavian (for English spelling reform) are famous examples.

twist.text: Some constructed scripts like Shavian were meant for real use—but failed to gain adoption.

climax.text: Constructed scripts show that writing systems can be designed—not just evolved organically.

punchline.text: If a language can be invented, so can its writing.
